**Author:** The Milk Man (@MrMilkTrading, verified; options/futures trader, Texas; milkmantrades.com) · posted 2026-08-31 12:28Z · received 2026-09-01T07:15:54Z (WhatsApp via RDP-30, routed by CoS). Credits @semoi69 for the original point.

## Summary
A methodological exchange on backtest validity:

- @semoi69's critique: **fixed 1-contract sizing distorts backtests across eras** — since 2022 a 200-pt Nasdaq move is normal (it was not in 2008); "would you still take a 1-contract bet at Nasdaq 70k with moves 3× bigger?"
- Milk Man's response: re-ran the backtest measuring **"points captured as % of notional"** — keeps exposure constant across trades. **Edge per unit of exposure still improved out of sample**, so the strategy holds up; he's adopting this as a standard step in future backtests.
- Attached: backtest chart (1639×2160).

Stats at capture: 4k views, 28 likes, 40 bookmarks.

## Why it matters
- Checklist-grade rule: **before accepting any backtest, normalize edge as % of notional (constant exposure).** Fixed-contract PnL conflates edge with regime drift — index level and volatility inflation since 2022 flatter recent samples and hide whether per-unit risk is actually paid.
- A regime-adjustment cousin of the v1.1 hardening checklist: joins "actual broker margins" and "stress cases not in historical data" as a pre-acceptance gate.
- Third Milk-ecosystem capture — the author iterates on *methodology* in public, not just setups.
